what_was_done:
Wrapped every DISPATCHING action handler in src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts with a precondition gate. The 38-case-branch enumeration in the bead description resolves to 37 actual case branches in the current codebase (operator memo line-counts drifted vs HEAD). Of those 37: 34 are DISPATCHING (mutate pipeline:* labels OR launch an agent OR mutate plan-state-class labels per the library's authoritative DISPATCHING_ACTIONS classification) and 3 are EXEMPT (stop-agent / human-approve / human-dismiss — only mutate human-decision-class labels OR stop a running agent). === IMPLEMENTATION ===
- Added `checkPreconditionsOrRefuse(params)` helper at the top of route.ts (just above POST). Helper builds DispatchContext via buildDispatchContext (re-using published readers — same TOCTOU window per Seam 4), evaluates predicates, and returns either null (proceed) or NextResponse with HTTP 412.
- 412 body merges buildPreconditionRefusalResponse output (refused, refusalCode, failedCheck, reason, observedState) with `action` and `epicId` per AC's required body shape (`{ refused: true, action, epicId, refusalCode, failedCheck, reason }`).
- `parsedWaveNumber` coerced once inside POST (before switch) so each case body can pass the same value into the helper without re-parsing.
- Each DISPATCHING case body starts with: `const refusal = await checkPreconditionsOrRefuse({ epicId, fleetCorePath, action: "<literal>", waveNumber: parsedWaveNumber }); if (refusal) return refusal;` — placed BEFORE any label mutation or agent launch (per bead AC + architecture § Component Boundaries Contract 1).
- Each EXEMPT case body has a one-line `// EXEMPT per beads_web-ehp.11: <reason>` comment immediately inside the case opener.
- Imports at top of file (line 35-44) reference the library; helper docstring cites the bead.

=== EXISTING TEST PRESERVATION ===
- Default `dispatch-preconditions` mock added to fleet-action.test.ts, fleet-action-qa.test.ts, route.skip-research.test.ts: `evaluatePreconditions` defaults to `{ ok: true }` so existing 200-OK paths preserved unchanged.
- All 132 + 49 + 23 = 204 existing tests pass after the wrap. No assertion shifts; no shape drift.

surprises_or_findings:
1. CASE COUNT DRIFT (memo vs codebase): The bead description and operator memo cite '38 case branches' at specific line numbers (526, 629, ..., 2868). Empirical grep of HEAD finds 37 case branches at slightly-shifted line numbers (e.g., the memo's line 2868 doesn't match any actual case opener; the closest is 'review-plan' at 2796). The memo's line-number list appears to be one short and slightly off due to interim commits between when the memo was authored and HEAD. I followed the LIBRARY's authoritative classification (DISPATCHING_ACTIONS = 34 elements; EXEMPT_ACTIONS = 3 elements) which sums to 37 — 1:1 with my codebase enumeration. Surfacing for operator awareness; no rework needed.

2. CLASSIFICATION AMBIGUITY (approve-plan): The bead's literal classification rule says 'EXEMPT if it only mutates human-decision:* labels OR sets observability flags OR stops a running agent; DISPATCHING if it mutates pipeline:* labels OR launches an agent.' The `approve-plan` case mutates ONLY plan:pending → plan:approved (plan:* labels, not pipeline:* and not human-decision:*) and does not launch an agent. By the rule's literal text, this case fits NEITHER category cleanly. The dispatch-preconditions library (ehp.13) classifies it as DISPATCHING because plan-label mutation gates downstream dispatch (start-wave / review-wave consume plan:approved). I followed the library's classification (no operator surface needed since the library is the architected source of truth) but flagging here per the bead's 'note any ambiguous classification' instruction. Recommendation for future: add 'OR mutates plan:* labels' to the bead's DISPATCHING rule for explicit coverage.

3. SIBLING-AGENT GIT RESETS DURING SESSION: While working this bead, two sibling commits landed on main (beads_web-ehp.10 dispatchChainAction wrap + beads_web-ehp.8 repeat-dispatch-escalation wrap) AND multiple `git reset --hard HEAD` operations were observed in `git reflog`. These resets WIPED my uncommitted route.ts edits TWICE during the session — confirmed via grep returning 0 matches for `checkPreconditionsOrRefuse` in route.ts after each reset, with `git diff src/app/api/fleet/action/route.ts | wc -l` returning 0. Recovered by re-applying all 34 wraps + 3 EXEMPT comments + helper + imports + parsedWaveNumber, then immediately `git add`-staging to reduce loss-window for any subsequent reset. No work lost in the final state. Risk-flag for fleet operators: in-flight builders should ideally have an exclusive lock on tracked-file paths to prevent sibling resets from clobbering their working tree. (Out-of-scope for this bead; flagging.)

4. PRECONDITION_TABLE COVERAGE: All 34 dispatching actions are registered in EXTENDED_PRECONDITION_TABLE per ehp.13 (DISPATCHING_ACTIONS array at dispatch-preconditions.ts:1074-1110). No coverage gaps observed. The library's `evaluatePreconditions` falls open with a console.warn for unregistered actions — that path is exercised only by EXEMPT_ACTIONS (which never call the helper anyway, per the wrap pattern). Belt-and-suspenders: even if a reconciler somehow dispatched an EXEMPT action through this gate, evaluatePreconditions would warn-and-pass rather than block.

5. EXISTING TEST MOCK STRATEGY: Mocking `@/lib/dispatch-preconditions` (rather than the underlying `bead-status-reader` / `marker-reader` modules) keeps the test mock surface minimal and aligned with how the route handler integrates with the library. Default ok=true mock plus per-test override via `mockEvaluatePreconditions.mockReturnValue(...)` keeps the new precondition-test file < 450 lines while exercising 5 representative refusal codes + EXEMPT-not-gated sanity + happy-path proceed sanity (9 tests total).
